title: JavaScript Prototypes Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict prototype-chain lookup, inherited methods, constructor prototypes, class prototype behavior, and prototype-related pitfalls.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which chain is correct for `const dog = new Dog()` where `class Dog extends Animal {}`?
questions.explanation: Instances inherit from the child prototype, which inherits from the parent prototype, then `Object.prototype`, then `null`.
Public fields become own properties on each instance. Class methods live on the prototype.

questions.explanation: `__proto__` is an object-level prototype accessor. A function's `.prototype` is the object assigned as prototype to instances created with `new`.
`Object.create(null)` creates an object with no prototype, so it does not inherit `toString`.
